loadConfig's tmp-state guard at line 99 (`if (!process.env.MUTATION_ALLOW_TMP_STATE)`) is the gate the helper default satisfies; verified with `env -u MUTATION_ALLOW_TMP_STATE node --test` from templates/mutation-incremental — 143/143 pass with the var unset at shell level, confirming the described fix works end-to-end.

configDigest() parses the raw config file and deletes raw.views before hashing canonicalJSON(raw), matching spec K3.4/§11.3 (views is read-time-only and must not affect the invalidation digest); config.mjs's own duplicate-key/shape validation runs separately in loadConfig, so this second parse in configDigest is redundant but not incorrect.

duplicateKey()'s escape-skip (`j += text[j] === '\\' ? 2 : 1`) only special-cases a 2-char jump for backslash escapes, but this is correct even for \uXXXX: skipping the backslash+u pair leaves the 4 trailing hex digits to be scanned normally, and hex digits can never be a quote or backslash, so the closing quote is still found correctly.

findings.note: lib/main.mjs's planCommand calls resolveViews(config, snapshot) strictly for its validation side effect (throwing on a bad views config) after computePlan() has already run and before the plan is serialized to stdout; the returned view map is discarded. Not a normal-usage failure (the plan output is unaffected and validation still happens before commands complete), but it reads as coincidental ordering rather than an intentional contract, worth a comment or restructure when Plan 1b wires in view summaries so a future edit doesn't assume resolveViews's return value already feeds the emitted plan.
